item.title: Ruihong Huang
item.description:
About

Dr. Ruihong (Ray) Huang is a Professor of geography in the Department of Geography, Planning, and Recreation at Northern Arizona University, where he has been a faculty member since 2003. His research focuses on GIS for urban transportation. He developed data models and schedule-base pathfinding algorithms for transit networks, and implemented the models and algorithms to online transit trip planners and urban accessibility studies.

Research Interests

Data models and pathfinding algorithms for transit network

  • Development of object-oriented models for dynamic transit networks
  • Database development for transit systems
  • Development of schedule-based pathfinding algorithms using Pattern-First Search
  • Development of web-based transit trip planners

Transit-facilitated urban accessibility

  • Understanding urban spatial structure and job accessibility
  • Simulating individual work trips of transit-dependent commuters
  • Developing individual trip-based accessibility index
  • Providing tools for individual work trip simulation

Spatial data analysis

  • Uncovering spatial patterns with Hidden Markov Model
  • Analyzing urban land use and job accessibility
  • Exploring national park accessibility and visitation
  • Exploring space-time pattern of national park visitor activities

item.title: Graduate Certificates
item.description:
Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Certificate

Program Overview

  • Delivery: Asynchronous Online
  • Credits: 16
  • Duration: Two semesters

Program Description

The Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Certificate prepares students to use geospatial technologies in professional settings. GIS provides a framework for collecting, managing, and analyzing spatial data, integrating multiple data types to create maps, visualizations, and 3D scenes. Through advanced coursework in GIS principles, enterprise geodatabases, geospatial programming, and web‑based GIS, students gain practical skills applicable to urban planning, cartography, remote sensing, and environmental resource management. Designed for post‑graduate learners entering the GIS field or adding geospatial analysis to their discipline, the certificate equips graduates for careers in landscape architecture, local government, scientific research, community health, surveying, and related fields.

Curriculum

  • GSP 520 - Principles of Remote Sensing
  • GSP 531 - Map Design and GIS
  • GSP 535 - Programming for GIS
  • GSP 536 - Enterprise Geodatabase Development and Applications
  • GSP 538 - Geographic Data Analysis
  • GSP 539 - Geovisualization
  • GSP 540 - GIS for Transprotation

Student Learning Outcomes:

  • Create, manipulate and manage geospatial data.
  • Perform spatial analysis to support spatial related decision making.
  • Develop GIS tools and automate geoprocessing.
  • Present and deliver geospatial information in online and professional quality formats.

Admission Requirements:

  • Transcripts
  • Undergraduate degree from a regionally accredited institution with 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent.

Contact Information

  • How to apply: Prof. Erik Schiefer: erik.schiefer@nau.edu
  • Curriculum: Prof. Ruihong Huang: ruihong.huang@nau.edu

Recreational Therapy Certificate

Program Overview

  • Delivery: Asynchronous Online
  • Credits: 18-21 total credit hours
  • Fieldwork: 40 hours of fieldwork or equivalent

Program Description

The Graduate Certificate in Recreational Therapy prepares students for the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification (NCTRC) exam and careers as Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialists. Therapeutic Recreation uses recreation and activity‑based interventions to enhance quality of life for people of all backgrounds. Practitioners work in hospitals, schools, behavioral health, corrections, long‑term care, community agencies, and outdoor programs. The curriculum aligns with all ten NCTRC job task domains, building skills in assessment, intervention planning, implementation, evaluation, documentation, teamwork, and program management. The certificate supports both the academic and professional eligibility pathways, providing the required coursework for national credentialing.

Curicculum

Take the following 18-21 units:

  • PRM 502, PRM 503, PRM 504, PRM 505, PRM 506, PRM 507 (18 units)
  • Students are required to complete 40 hours of fieldwork, with consultation of the advisor. This may be through paid or unpaid work experiences, through additional field experiences in courses, or by completing one of the following courses (0-3 units):
    • PRM 525 (0 - 3 units)
    • PRM 555 (0 - 3 units)
    • PRM 608 (0 - 3 units)

Student Learning Outcomes

  • Demonstrate entry-level knowledge of the therapeutic recreation profession in history, theory, philosophy, and sciences and the scope and practices of recreation therapy/therapeutic recreation across diverse delivery systems.
  • Demonstrate the ability to assess, plan, implement, document, and evaluate therapeutic recreation services that facilitate targeted outcomes, and that embrace personal and cultural dimensions of diversity (including international application of recreational therapy).
  • Demonstrate entry-level knowledge and competence of the theories, principles, and practices of management/administration of therapeutic recreation services.

Admission Requirements

  • Transcripts
  • Undergraduate degree from a regionally accredited institution with a 3.0 GPA on 4.0 scale or the equivalent.
